endorsements.quote: System design should encourage appropriate reliance on AI by supporting critical evaluation, preventing automation bias, and discouraging algorithm aversion.
CADx systems should provide clear feedback on processing status and diagnostic confidence to support informed decision-making and prevent misinterpretation of system outputs.
AI-generated explanations should be presented in a clear, structured, and clinically relevant manner to support accurate interpretation and reduce the risk of misunderstanding.

unlisted_practices: Enable clinicians to request additional explanations or clarification on demand through interactive interface elements.
Align outputs from multiple explainable AI methods, present them coherently, and clearly indicate discrepancies between them.
Present information in a structured, non-overwhelming manner that integrates relevant patient data and explanations to minimize clinician cognitive load.
Use STPA-based hazard analysis of clinician-AI interaction to derive traceable safety requirements for AI diagnostic systems.
Use agreement between multiple explainable AI methods as a signal to flag potentially unreliable predictions and trigger clinician prompts or warnings.

screen.reason: The paper presents a methodology and set of safety design guidelines/framework (derived via System-Theoretic Process Analysis) for clinician-AI interaction in computer-aided diagnosis systems rather than reporting an empirical deployment or reader study evaluation.
